The decoder reaches the fixed-subframe residual path that uses the bitreader to consume Rice-coded partitions.
Residual partition headers are read directly from the attacker-controlled bitstream.
The Rice decoder snapshots its current consumed-word cursor before decoding each partition's signed residuals.
Residual symbol decoding reads the current buffered word, so exhaustion of the buffer makes the indexed access critical.
As repeated residual values are decoded, the cursor advances toward the end of the available buffered data.
The sink is the final indexed buffer read when another residual bit read is attempted from an exhausted position.
